Although the keyword *upāsaka* (lay devotee) appears frequently throughout Buddhist literature and secondary scholarship, none of the surveyed reference passages discuss or cite this particular discourse.
According to SuttaCentral, passage-level parallels to the verse of this sutta are preserved across multiple traditions in the thirty-eighth or thirtieth chapter (*Sukhavarga*) of the *Udānavarga*, including the Sanskrit recensions (UV 30; UVS 30), the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (Uv Kg 30, "Happiness"), and two Chinese versions in the Taishō canon (T 212.31 and T 213.30, *Faji yaosong jing*) [SuttaCentral].
